Socio-economic drivers of health, England & Wales

2011 and 2021 Census, 348 local authorities (323 matched across both censuses). Code and full write-up on GitHub

270 of 323areas reported better health in 2021 than 2011 (mean +0.63 pp)
Catch-upareas that were less healthy in 2011 improved more (r = -0.23)
28%of the variation in change explained on held-out areas; age structure, not in this data, is a likely missing factor
48 areasform a distinct diverse, high-migration cluster: London and large cities

How to use: drag a box on the PCA plot, or click any area (shift-click for several), and the same areas light up in every view. Double-click to clear. The region menu filters everything, and the variable menu colours the first map by any of the 20 Census variables. Scroll to zoom and drag to pan on the t-SNE, catch-up and model-fit plots; double-click resets them. Hover for exact values. Grey areas on the change map are councils merged between 2019 and 2021, which have no like-for-like 2021 figure.

Data: ONS 2011 and 2021 Census via Nomis; boundaries: ONS Open Geography Portal, Local Authority Districts (December 2011). Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 and OS data © Crown copyright and database right. Built with Python and Altair.
